title: Sapiom template gallery registry
description: Thin gallery index for the onboarding template gallery (SAP-1263). The single edit point: add a template here and it appears in the UI gallery. The Sapiom backend reads this file at a pinned ref, validates it, computes estimated cost from `capabilities`, and expands `steps` into a definition graph for the inspect view.

id.description: Stable gallery id + the example directory name. Never changes — it is the directory name, the sourcePath, and the gallery's stable key. Renaming a template changes `name`, never this.

name.description: Display name shown on the card. Names the OUTCOME, not the machinery — the same axis `category` uses. No arrows, no slashes, no parentheticals, and no mechanism word (saga, engine, pipeline, runner, endpoint, gate, durable, keep-alive): those belong in `tags`, which is what drives search. Enforced by the `copy-name` check.

description.description: One-line card description — one plain sentence.

rank.description: Optional gallery ordering weight — lower = higher priority. Ranked templates lead the browse gallery in ascending rank; unranked templates keep registry (id) order behind them. Used to feature the strongest templates up front; most templates carry none. The backend owns the sort (single source of truth), so the frontend adds no sort of its own. Independent of `category` grouping and of runnability — a rank is an editorial choice, not a derived signal.

onboarding.description: First-impression (onboarding shelf) curation, owned HERE so the app never hard-codes template ids. The bar is STRICTER than the gallery's `setup.runsWithNoSetup`: a clean, side-effect-free, zero-setup run that leaves a REAL, impressive artifact worth showing a brand-new user — set only after verifying it against a fresh tenant. `eligible` gates membership in the onboarding suggestion pool; `order` is the shelf sequence (lower leads), independent of the gallery `rank`.

eligible.description: True only when a fresh-tenant zero-setup run was verified to leave a real, impressive artifact. Absent = not eligible; never assert without evidence.

order.description: Onboarding shelf priority — lower leads the first-run grid. First-impression sequence, NOT browse ordering, so it is deliberately separate from `rank`. Eligible templates without an order sort after ordered ones.

category.description: Primary gallery category (the source-of-truth taxonomy). Exactly one per template; the frontend owns the display label, icon, and section order keyed off this id. The axis is OUTCOME — "what am I trying to produce?" — not mechanism: `starter` aside, a template belongs to the business job it does, never to the primitive it demonstrates. Mechanism words (durable, pause-resume, hitl, evals, media, orchestration) stay in freeform `tags`, which drive secondary browse/search. Optional for now — every template should carry one, and the examples CI check flags any invalid value.

discipline.description: The one-or-two-word FUNCTION shown on the card's badge — who owns this outcome. Finer than `category`, on the same OUTCOME axis: `category` groups the gallery rail, `discipline` labels the individual card, so two templates in one category routinely carry different disciplines (both `pr-review-bot` and `dependency-upgrade` are `product-engineering`; only the second is `Release engineering`). Human-readable and rendered VERBATIM — unlike `category`, this is not an id the app relabels. The app owns only the glyph beside it. Must be one of the disciplines allowed for this row's `category`, a cross-field constraint JSON Schema cannot express and `examples:check` therefore gates; the enum here is the union across all categories, not the set valid for any one of them. Optional — a template without one falls back to a short label derived from its `category`, so the badge never disappears.

complexity.description: How much VARIATION AND JUDGMENT is in this template's output — authored, not derived from the graph. The axis is not graph size: a deterministic saga with a wide fan-out is `simple` (its answer is always approve/reject), while two chained model steps are not (each one's output is the next one's input, so drift compounds). Count the points where something non-deterministic is produced — a model call, a generated image or video, a capability that synthesizes prose for you — then nudge up one band, never more, when the scaffolding around them is heavy or their output drives something irreversible. See AUTHORING.md §3 for the rubric. Optional for now — every template should carry one, and the examples CI check nudges any that don't. The check also validates the enum and warns when the authored band sits 2+ bands from the score derived from `steps[].kind` / `capabilities`, which means either the label or the declared shape is wrong.

cadence.description: What STARTS a run — the gallery's "Trigger" fact. Describes the entry only, not what the run does mid-flight: `wait-for-webhook` is `on-demand` (you start it; it pauses for a callback partway through), whereas `pr-review-bot` is `on-webhook` (the PR event itself starts it). Use `on-event` for a run invoked by an endpoint the template deploys.

sourcePath.description: Path of the example inside this repo (e.g. `examples/<id>`), consumed by the fork + MCP clone handoff.

capabilities.description: Declared catalog capability ids (dotted, e.g. `web.search`). Drives the estimated per-run cost without a built definition.

steps.description: Declared graph, rendered on the inspect view. Array order is execution order; the first step is the entry.

setup.description: Runnability summary for the gallery shelf. Denormalised from the co-located template.json ON PURPOSE — the shelf renders from listTemplates, which never fetches manifests, so a shelf that needed the manifest would be N+1. Generated by `pnpm examples:sync-setup`; never hand-maintained. The third shelf state, "pauses for your approval", is deliberately NOT here: it is already derivable from `steps[].checkpoint`, which the examples CI check enforces.

runsWithNoSetup.description: True ONLY when a measured run proved the template reaches a meaningful terminal state with zero input and zero credentials. Defaults false — never assert it without evidence.

connectionCount.description: Number of `requiredSecrets` entries in the manifest. Drives "needs 1 credential to do anything real".

settingCount.description: Number of declared `settings` (all of which have defaults).

provisions.description: Managed resource kinds the run provisions, driving the cost disclosure on the card. DERIVED from the manifest's `resources[]` — the distinct kinds, sorted. Never hand-maintained: the `setup-provisions` check fails when this disagrees with the manifest, which is what stops the drift that let `capabilities[]` fill up with SDK method paths instead of catalog ids.

degradedWithoutSetup.description: Mirrors `zeroSetup.narrative` from the manifest. Rendered verbatim on the card — the shelf must never imply a send that will not happen.

capability.description: Catalog capability id this step calls, or null/omitted for an in-process step.

kind.description: What the step structurally IS, which picks its glyph in the rendered graph. `capability` calls a priced catalog capability; `llm` calls a model (`llm.run` / `models.run` / `models.coding`); `compute` is in-process logic, a branch, or a terminal; `pause` suspends the run at $0 until something wakes it. A step that both calls a capability and then suspends is `pause` — suspending is the step's defining behaviour.

checkpoint.description: True when this step is a HUMAN decision gate — a person must approve before the run proceeds. Strictly narrower than `kind: "pause"`: most pauses are machine waits (a render job, a webhook callback, a drip interval) and must NOT be marked, or the gallery will advertise "waiting for a video to encode" as an approval boundary. Set it only where a person decides; most templates have none. At most one per template — the examples CI check enforces both rules.

next.description: Names of steps this step continues to.

terminal.description: True when this step is a sink (ends the run).
